s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva with a gradual increase in number over time
salient_findings: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age and gradually increased
Family history of similar facial papules
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules are present on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Lesions gradually increased to approximately 60
Patient has a medical history of meningioma
Family history is notable for a daughter with similar facial papules
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
Histopathology showed buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
Whole-exome sequencing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene

shortlist.label: nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: multiple dome-shaped skin-colored papules, family history of similar lesions, and genetic mutation in SUFU gene

shortlist.label: trichoepithelioma
shortlist.why_kept: multiple skin-colored papules on the face, histopathology showing buds and cords of basaloid cells

shortlist.label: trichodiscoma
shortlist.why_kept: skin-colored papules, histopathology consistent with trichodiscoma

shortlist.label: syringoma
shortlist.why_kept: multiple small skin-colored papules, particularly on the face and vulva

shortlist.label: basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: skin-colored papules, histopathology showing basaloid cells, and genetic mutation in SUFU gene

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva, along with a history of meningioma and a family history of similar lesions, combined with the histopathological findings and the genetic mutation in the SUFU gene, are all consistent with nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome.

rejected.label: trichoepithelioma
rejected.why: While trichoepithelioma can present with similar skin lesions, the combination of the patient's meningioma, family history, and genetic findings are more specific for nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome.

rejected.label: trichodiscoma
rejected.why: Trichodiscoma typically presents as a solitary lesion and does not account for the patient's broader clinical and genetic picture.

rejected.label: syringoma
rejected.why: Syringoma usually presents as smaller, more translucent lesions, often around the eyes, and does not typically involve the vulva or include the other features seen in this patient.

rejected.label: basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While basal cell carcinoma can present with skin-colored papules, the multiplicity, location, and genetic findings in this case are more suggestive of nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome.
